client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: A nurse reports work-related back strain and participates in an ergonomic job assessment. What is the primary purpose of this assessment?

options.A: Identify job and workplace risk factors for musculoskeletal injury so appropriate controls can be developed
options.B: Determine whether the nurse should stop using available patient-handling equipment
options.C: Evaluate only office workstation factors because ergonomics does not apply to direct patient care
options.D: Confirm that physical strain is unavoidable and cannot be reduced through workplace changes

rationale: NIOSH describes ergonomics programs as systematic approaches for identifying, analyzing, and controlling workplace risk factors for work-related musculoskeletal disorders. Job analysis considers tasks, physical demands, postures, layouts, and other contributing factors so risk-reduction controls can be developed. Therefore A is correct. Ergonomic assessment applies to healthcare work, complements rather than replaces safe patient-handling equipment, and is specifically intended to identify modifiable risks.
educational_objective: Recognize ergonomic assessment as a process for identifying workplace musculoskeletal risk factors and guiding controls that reduce worker injury.
source_organization: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
